entry.title: Re: QM Control Key not updating in Purchase Order from Ma...
entry.content:
The QM control key on a PO item is a copy, not a live link to the material master. It is copied when the material is taken into the item and then it stays on the item (field EKPO-SSQSS). So a change in the material master does not change POs that already exist, and on a new PO the key depends on two settings, not one. I read the standard PO code and ran BAPI_PO_CREATE1 in test mode (TESTRUN, nothing saved) in an S/4HANA 2023 system. This is what it does:

1. Where the key comes from

The copy is in FORM UEBERNAHME_MATERIAL (include MM06EF0U_UEBERNAHME_MATERIAL), when the material is taken into the item:

  • It only runs when the flag QM in Procurement Is Active is set (MARA-QMPUR, general material data, not per plant; the PO reads it as MT06E-QMPUR). If the flag is not set, the item gets no key at all, whatever is maintained for the plant.
  • With the flag set, the item gets the control key of its own plant (MARC-SSQSS, read as MT06E-SSQSS) and the certificate type.
  • With the flag set and no key in that plant, the PO stops with QB 114 "Define QM procurement key & (material &)". For an RFQ it is only a warning.
  • The QM info record (table QINF) has no control key field, so the key does not come from there.

2. What the test run showed

  • A material with the flag set and key 0000 in the plant, no key sent: the item came back with 0000. A second material with key 0009 in the same plant came back with 0009.
  • The first material again, now sending CTRL_KEY 0001 (with the X in POITEMX): the item kept 0001 instead of the master value, and the run stopped with 06 889 "No QM info record exists for material &", because 0001 is Supplier release and needs a QM info record. So a key sent by an interface or a BAPI is taken as it comes, and then the checks of that key run.

3. Changing the key on an existing PO

The screen field check is FORM QM_CHANGE_SSQSS (include MM06EFQM). It accepts only the key that is in the material master for that plant right now, or the key the item already had. Anything else stops with ME 554 "Control key & cannot be used here", and while the master has a key you cannot clear it either. The code comment says it plainly: the key can only be changed if the material is maintained for QM in procurement in that plant, so MARA-QMPUR and MARC-SSQSS must be set. After a valid change it runs the QM info record check for the new key.

What I would do

  • In MM03, check the QM view: the flag QM in Procurement Is Active and the Control Key for the plant of the PO item. The key is per plant, so a PO for another plant takes that plant's key.
  • For POs created before the master change: change the master first, then in ME22N enter the new key on each item (field Control Key in the item detail; screen structure MEPO1313, the same one that holds the over and underdelivery tolerances, stock type and GR based flag). It passes the check because it now matches the master.
  • For many items: BAPI_PO_CHANGE with CTRL_KEY in POITEM and the X in POITEMX (both fields exist in BAPIMEPOITEM and BAPIMEPOITEMX). The new key still goes through its own checks, so a key with supplier release needs the QM info record first.
  • If new POs get a wrong key, check first whether they come from an interface or a BAPI that fills CTRL_KEY, since that value wins over the master.

Not tested: I did not change a material master and then open an old PO, because that lab has no PO item for a material with QM in procurement (52 material and plant records with a key, and no PO item with a key at all). So "old items keep the old key" comes from the code, not from a run. I also did not run ME22N in dialog, so the ME 554 rule is read from the code, and I did not run BAPI_PO_CHANGE.

entry.title: Re: Austria - Down Payment Process in SAP Cloud ERP
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question. Here's the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you solve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Problem Summary

  • FAZ vs. F2/LR Tax Treatment Gap (AT→AT): In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the standard scope item BJK uses condition type TTX1 with access sequence TTX1. For domestic scenarios (e.g., AT→AT), Requirement 7 fires on the first access and reads condition table A002 using Departure Country, Customer Tax Classification, and Material Tax Classification — with no Billing Category differentiation. This means a Down Payment Request (FAZ, Billing Category P) receives the same tax code as a standard invoice (F2) or credit memo (LR), making it impossible out of the box to assign a deferred tax code specifically to FAZ documents in domestic scenarios. [1] [2]

  • Requirement 8 Blocking A165 for Domestic Cases: The second access in TTX1 — which reads condition table A165 (which includes Billing Category as a key field) — is governed by Requirement 8. Requirement 8 explicitly checks that departure country and destination country are not identical (and are not an intra-EU domestic equivalent). If either country field is empty or both are the same, the requirement is not fulfilled, and the access to A165 is skipped entirely. For AT→AT, this means the Billing Category field in A165 is structurally inaccessible for domestic tax differentiation. [1] [2]

Solutions Explored
Approach Feasibility Notes
Custom Access Sequence (e.g., ZTX1)Feasible — Recommended PathSAP explicitly supports creating a custom condition type (e.g., ZTX1) copied from TTX1, with a custom access sequence (e.g., ZTX1) that includes a new condition table with the required key fields. For the purchasing side, this is documented step-by-step. The same principle applies to SD: create a custom access that fires for domestic scenarios and includes Billing Category as a key field, without Requirement 8 blocking it. [3] [4]
Standard SAP Configuration (TTX1 out of the box)Not sufficient for this use caseThe standard TTX1 access sequence does not support domestic Billing Category differentiation. Requirement 8 on the A165 access is designed for export/EU scenarios only. No standard configuration switch exists to make A165 accessible for AT→AT without modifying the access sequence. [1] [2] [5]
SAP Support / OSS NotePartially relevant — no direct fix note identifiedKBA 3308072 documents the TTX1 determination logic in detail and confirms the Requirement 8 behavior. KBA 3480098 confirms tax code determination via condition records in billing. KBA 3712216 shows a precedent where a custom condition table with different key fields was the recommended resolution for a tax classification mismatch. No specific OSS note addressing the AT domestic FAZ deferred tax gap via a standard fix has been identified in available sources. [1] [6] [7]
Recommended Resolution

The most viable path — consistent with SAP's own documented extensibility approach for tax code determination in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition — is the custom access sequence route:

  1. Create a Custom Condition Table (e.g., Table Z65 or 999) with key fields: Departure Country, Destination Country, Billing Category, Customer Tax Classification, Material Tax Classification. Use Configuration Step ID 102890 ("Create Condition Table") in your configuration environment. Generate the table after defining the fields. [3]

  2. Create a Custom Access Sequence (e.g., ZTX1) via Configuration Step ID 102889 ("Define Access Sequence"). Add accesses in the following order:

    • Access 1: New domestic access pointing to your custom table (Z65/999), with a requirement that fires when departure country = destination country (i.e., a domestic-equivalent of Requirement 7 logic), and includes Billing Category as a key field. This allows FAZ (Billing Category P) to be differentiated from F2/LR.
    • Access 2: Standard domestic access to A002 (for F2/LR without Billing Category match).
    • Access 3: Export access to A165 with Requirement 8 (retained for cross-border scenarios). [3] [4]

  3. Create a Custom Condition Type (e.g., ZTX1) by copying TTX1 via Configuration Step ID 101094 ("Set Pricing Condition Types"). Assign your new access sequence ZTX1. Do not change any other control fields — they are critical for the condition to function as a tax determination condition. [3]

  4. Create a Custom Pricing Procedure (e.g., Z10021) by copying the standard procedure (e.g., A10021) via Configuration Step ID 101095 ("Set Calculation Schema"). Replace TTX1 with ZTX1 on the tax determination step. [3]

  5. Assign the Custom Pricing Procedure to the relevant billing/sales document types for Austria (domestic scenarios) via the pricing procedure determination configuration.

  6. Maintain Condition Records using the "Set Tax Rates – Sales" app. For your custom condition table, create entries for:

    • Billing Category P (FAZ) → assign your deferred tax code (e.g., AT_DEF)
    • No Billing Category entry (or Billing Category blank/F2) → assign the standard tax code [4] [6]

  7. Configure Deferred Tax Codes in the Define Tax Codes for Sales and Purchases activity. Define a deferred tax code and a target tax code, and enter the target tax code in the Target Tax Code field of the deferred tax code properties. [8]

  8. Configure Deferred Tax Processing for Austria using the Customizing activity /SAPPCE/KWF1_BUKRS (T-Code SM30), path: Financial Accounting → Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable → Business Transactions → Debit-Side and Credit-Side Down Payment Chains → Deferred Tax for Down Payment Chains → Customizing for Deferred Tax. Enter Company Code, Document Type, auxiliary Account, Migration Date, and set the "Impact of Final Invoice" flag — which is specifically relevant for Germany and Austria, where there is a change from deferral-based to accrual-based taxation after the final invoice.

  9. Test in Quality System before transporting to production. Validate pricing analysis for FAZ (Billing Category P) to confirm the deferred tax code is hit on the new domestic access, and for F2/LR to confirm the standard tax code is determined via the fallback access. [3]

SAP Support Experience
  • KBA 3308072 is the primary reference for understanding TTX1 determination logic in SD billing for S/4HANA Cloud. It explicitly documents Requirement 7 and Requirement 8 behavior and confirms that A165 (with Billing Category) is only accessible under Requirement 8 (export). This is the authoritative confirmation of the gap you have identified. [1] [2]
  • KBA 3480098 confirms the general tax code determination mechanism via condition records in billing documents and is useful for troubleshooting pricing analysis. [6]
  • KBA 3712216 provides a direct precedent: when a condition type was using the wrong access sequence/key fields for tax classification, SAP's resolution was to define a new condition table with the correct key fields and assign it to the access sequence — exactly the approach recommended here. [7]
  • The Austria-specific deferred tax configuration path (including the "Impact of Final Invoice" setting for AT) is documented in the SAP Help Portal under Austria → Finance → Tax Calculation and Tax Management → Processing VAT → Deferred Tax Processing. [8]

No standard SAP note delivering an out-of-the-box fix for the domestic FAZ deferred tax gap in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition has been identified. The extensibility path (custom access sequence + condition table) is the SAP-endorsed approach for this type of requirement. [3] [4]

Sources:

  • [1] 3308072 - Output tax determination in sales billing - SAP S/4HANA CloudSAP Support User Applications
  • [2] Output tax determination in sales billing - SAP S/4HANA CloudSAP Community
  • [3] SAP S/4HANA Cloud: Determine Tax Code in Purchase Documents using Condition TechniqueSAP Community
  • [4] Determining Tax Code in Purchase Documents using Pricing Conditions | SAP Help PortalSAP Help
  • [6] 3480098 - Tax Code Determination in Billing Document - SAP S/4HANA CloudSAP Support User Applications
  • [7] 3712216 - Incorrect tax classification determined for condition type TES1 in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public EditionSAP Support User Applications
  • [8] Configuring Tax Codes for Deferred Tax | SAP Help PortalSAP Help

entry.title: BTP Transports with CTMS & Content Agent | Part 5: Transporting role collections
entry.content:
Part 5 of the series BTP Transports with CTMS & Content Agent.

In Part 4 the first integration package travelled from Dev to Central. In this part we reuse the same CTMS landscape for something different: role collections. This time the export does not start in Integration Suite but in the Content Agent UI.

What travels with a role collection

According to SAP's list of supported content types, a role collection is transported together with its users, role mappings, custom roles, user groups and attribute mappings. Keep that in mind: if a role collection is assigned to users in Dev, those assignments go along (more on that below).

Step 1: Content Agent UI and your user in Dev

  • In Dev, subscribe to Content Agent Service with the free plan. This is the UI.
  • Your user needs a role collection for the Content Agent UI, plus the role Content Agent Secure Content Operator. In the role picker it shows up as Security Operator. I simply added it to the transport role collection from Part 4.

Step 2: Activate the Role Collections content type

Open the Content Agent UI and go to Content Types. Role Collections first shows Action Recommended. Activate it and a wizard called Create Destination for Role Collections starts:

  1. Login: your Cloud Foundry credentials or a one-time passcode.
  2. Environment: pick the Cloud Foundry org and space.
  3. Review and Complete: the wizard creates an SAP Authorization and Trust Management Service instance (plan apiaccess), its key and the destination XSUAARoleCollections for you.

Afterwards Role Collections shows Active. SAP Help also describes the manual way (API credentials from the btp CLI and a destination with the fixed name XSUAARoleCollections), but the wizard did it in one go.

The last step of the wizard in my setup.

Step 3: Prepare Central for importing

  • The Content Agent instance in Central from Part 3 (plan application) needs a second role next to Import: Content Agent Secure Content Operator. Update the instance and add it. Without it the import fails (see below).
  • SAP Help describes the same XSUAARoleCollections destination for the account where you import, so set it up in Central as well (wizard or manual).

Step 4: Export from the Content Agent UI

  1. In the Content Agent UI in Dev, choose Export.
  2. Add Content: select the role collection. You see its roles, users and user groups underneath.
  3. Export Details: Export Mode SAP Cloud Transport Management, Create a New Transport Request, pick the source node and enter a description.
  4. Review and Export. The progress list ends with the transport request created in CTMS.

Export Details in my setup (source node blurred).

Step 5: Import and check

In CTMS, import the request on the target node, just like in Part 4. Then check the result in Central under Security > Role Collections and on the users who had the collection in Dev.

What tripped me up in my setup

  • The first import failed. The CTMS import log said: "Bad Request. To Import xsuaa content, Security operator Role is required." The integration package imports from Part 4 had worked with the same setup, because role collections are security content and need the extra role. We updated the Content Agent instance in Central and added the Security Operator role (SAP Help calls it Content Agent Secure Content Operator and lists it as a prerequisite for importing role collections). It was also added to the role collection of the user in Dev.
  • Users came along. Our test role collection was assigned to a user in Dev, and after the import the same user had it in Central. That is useful for a test, but in a real landscape decide before exporting whether Dev assignments should reach the next system.
  • We gave role collections their own lane. In our landscape role collections have their own source node, target node and route, separate from integration packages. That keeps security content and integration content in different import queues.
  • The yellow warning is not an error. On Export Details the UI says "The selected Cloud Transport Management destination has no open transport request." It only means there is nothing to add to yet. Choose Create a New Transport Request.
  • A side note on API Management. On the same Content Types screen, activating SAP API Management failed with "Error TTL001: The activation of API Composition for API Management failed". The message points to SAP Note 2904202. It did not affect role collections.

Roles for this part

WhoNeedsWhere
Your user (export)Content Agent UI role collection + Content Agent Secure Content OperatorDev
Content Agent instance (import)Import + Content Agent Secure Content OperatorCentral
Whoever importsCTMS ImportOperator (Part 4)Central

What comes next

Role collections now travel too. In Part 6 we transport destinations, and look at what Content Agent deliberately leaves behind: passwords and secrets.

entry.title: Re: Making insight tiles available for other users
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question. Here's an AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,
Henrike

Sharing Dashboard Tiles with Other Users in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

You are not missing something fundamental — this is a genuine pain point that many administrators encounter. The short answer is: personal "Save as Tile" tiles are by design only visible to the user who created them, but SAP does provide a structured, role-based approach to share tiles broadly without necessarily requiring custom CDS views or KPI development. Here is how it works.

Why Personal Tiles Are Not Visible to Others

When you use "Save as Tile" from within an app, the tile is saved as a personal bookmark tied to your user session and your personal space. This is intentional — it is a personalization feature, not an administration feature. [1] [2]

The tile captures your current filter state and app context, and stores it as a dynamic tile (with counters etc.) on your launchpad. However, this tile lives in your personal scope and is not transported or shared to other users' launchpads automatically. [2]

SAP-Intended Approach for Shared Dashboards

SAP's intended mechanism for distributing tiles to groups of users is through the Spaces and Pages framework, combined with Business Roles and Business Catalogs: 

  • A Space represents an area of work and is assigned to one or more Business Roles.
  • A Page sits inside a Space and contains sections with tiles/apps.
  • Tiles on a page are derived from the Business Catalogs assigned to the Business Role linked to that Space. 

This means: if you want a tile to appear for all your logistics users, it must be:

  1. Defined as a tile in a Business Catalog, and
  2. That catalog must be assigned to the Business Role your logistics users have, and
  3. That Business Role must be linked to the Space/Page you have created. [5] 

The tools you use for this in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition are:

  • Manage Launchpad Spaces (app F4834)
  • Manage Launchpad Pages (app F4512)
  • Maintain Business Roles

These require the business catalog SAP_CORE_BC_UI_FLD and the SAP_BR_ADMINISTRATOR role. [5]

How to Share Existing App Tiles (Without Custom Development)

For standard SAP-delivered apps (e.g., standard logistics Fiori apps), you can share them without any custom development:

  1. Add the standard app tile to your Page via the Manage Launchpad Pages app. When editing a page, you can add sections and add tiles — the available tiles are those from the Business Catalogs assigned to the Business Role linked to the Space. 

  2. Assign the Space to the relevant Business Role in the Maintain Business Roles app. All users with that Business Role will then see the Space and its Pages. [5] [6]

  3. Publish and transport — when you create or modify Spaces and Pages, they are transported using the Adaptation Transport Organizer (ATO), which must be configured and activated. [5]

For standard apps that already support dynamic tiles (counters, live data), these will work for all users once the tile is placed on a shared page and the users have the correct role/catalog assignment. [7]

Key insight: The tiles you see on a shared page are role-based and catalog-driven — not personal bookmarks. So the "counter" behavior you love from your personal tiles is available on shared pages too, as long as the underlying app supports dynamic tiles and the service (e.g., DYNAMIC_TILE_SRV) is configured. [7]

When Custom Development Is Actually Needed

Custom CDS views, Analytical Queries, and KPIs are needed in specific scenarios, not as the default path for sharing standard tiles: [8] [9]

Scenario Custom Development Needed?
Sharing a standard SAP Fiori app tile with filters to all users❌ No — use Spaces/Pages + Business Role assignment
Creating a dynamic counter tile for a standard app❌ No — configure via Business Catalog and dynamic tile service
Reporting on data not covered by any standard CDS view✅ Yes — Custom CDS View required
Building a KPI tile with custom thresholds and measures✅ Yes — Custom Analytical Query + Manage KPIs and Reports app
Publishing a Query Browser report as a shared tile✅ Yes — use View Browser to publish as a Fiori app, then assign via catalog [10]

The View Browser approach (referenced in [8] and ) is worth noting: if you have built a custom analytical query, you can use the View Browser app to create an application from it and publish it as a tile to a Business Catalog — making it available to all users with that catalog, without it being a flat list. [8]

Summary

You do not need to go down the custom CDS/KPI route just to share standard app tiles. The correct SAP-intended path is:

  1. Use Manage Launchpad Pages to build your logistics dashboard page with standard app tiles.
  2. Assign the page to a Space, and assign the Space to the Business Role your logistics users hold.
  3. Ensure the Business Catalogs for those apps are assigned to the same Business Role.

entry.title: Re: unable to cancel activity confirmation
entry.content:
This message comes from the CO document of the reversal, not from the confirmation itself. When you cancel a confirmation, the reversal is posted with the posting date of the original confirmation (AFRU-BUDAT) as long as that period is not locked, and the CO document (activity allocation) gets the entry date, today, as document date. So a confirmation posted in 2025 and cancelled now gives posting date 2025 and document date 2026, and that is BK 098 "Document date and posting date are in different fiscal years". I checked it in an S/4HANA 2023 system, in the code and with a test run that saved nothing:

1. Where the two dates come from

  • CO_RU_CANCEL_PREPARE reads the confirmation to be cancelled and calls CO_RU_CHECK_PERIOD_BLOCKED with its original posting date.
  • CO_RU_CHECK_PERIOD_BLOCKED checks the CO period lock for business transaction RKL (actual activity allocation, OKP1). It checks the FI period (OB52) only if message RU 428 is set to E in table T160M. In that system there is no entry for RU 428, so only the CO lock counts.
  • CO_RI_CONF_CANCEL, which both cancel BAPIs call (BAPI_NETWORK_CONF_CANCEL and BAPI_ALM_CONF_CANCEL), uses the posting date you pass only when that check says the period is locked. Otherwise the reversal keeps the original date.
  • The document date is the entry date. In that system all 6 CO documents created by confirmations have document date equal to the entry date and posting date equal to the confirmation date, for example posting date 30.12.2024 with document date 31.12.2024.

2. What the test showed

That system has no network confirmation with a CO document, and every order with old confirmations that posted costs is already technically completed or closed, so I could not cancel one. Instead I posted a new time confirmation with BAPI_ALM_CONF_CREATE on an open maintenance order operation (PM and network confirmations both live in AFRU and post their costs as RKL), without COMMIT and with ROLLBACK WORK at the end:

  • Posting date 15.12.2025, entered today: BK 098 "Document date and posting date are in different fiscal years".
  • Same entry with today as posting date: no BK 098.
  • With TESTRUN = X neither date showed BK 098, so the check only runs in the real posting.
  • In that system BK 098 came back as information, and what stopped the cost posting was CK 466, no price for the internal activity in 2025.

What I would do

  • Look at all the messages of the cancellation, not only the date one. If BK 098 is only information or warning there and the error is something else for the old year (like the activity price in KP26), fix that and the reversal can post in the old period.
  • If you want the reversal in the current year instead, the period of the original confirmation has to be locked for RKL in OKP1 (or closed in OB52 with RU 428 set to E). Then the cancellation takes a new posting date and both dates are in the same year. With the BAPI, pass POSTG_DATE: it is only used in that case.
  • This fits what you see in QAS: old periods are often left open there. In a system where 2025 is already locked, the reversal does not go back to the old date.

Not tested: I did not run CN29 in dialog, so I did not see how it asks for the new posting date when the period is locked, and I did not cancel an old confirmation with costs. "The reversal keeps the original posting date" comes from the code, and BK 098 for different fiscal years comes from the test with a new confirmation. I also did not check if BK 098 is an error instead of information in other releases.

entry.title: Re: Unable to find Create Inbound Delivery -App ID VL31N
entry.content:
Root Cause Analysis

The SUPER YOU Starter System is a pre-configured, non-production S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition trial system. Even with the correct role and catalog assigned, the following factors can prevent the app from appearing:

1. Scope item 2TX (Direct Procurement with Inbound Delivery) may not be activated

In S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the Create Inbound Delivery (VL31N) app only becomes available when scope item 2TX – Direct Procurement with Inbound Delivery is active in the solution scope. If 2TX is not activated in the starter system, the business catalog SAP_LE_BC_ID_PROC_MC itself will not be present in the system, even though it appears in the Fiori Apps Reference Library.

Check: Open the Business Catalogs app and search for SAP_LE_BC_ID_PROC_MC. If it does not appear at all, the scope item is not activated.

Reference: SAP KBA 3462922 – Missing Business Catalogs and Business Role Templates confirms that a catalog remains inaccessible if its scope item has not been activated.

2. Role generation may be out of sync (KBA 3499342 / 3534671)

Even if the catalog is assigned to a role, the role's authorization objects may not have been generated for that tenant. This is documented in:

  • KBA 3499342 – Apps cannot be found after adding the business catalog
  • KBA 3534671 – Apps can't be found even though roles and catalogs are assigned

Workaround: In the Maintain Business Roles app, remove the business catalog from the role, save, then re-add it and save again. This forces re-generation of the role's authorizations. After that, log off and back in.

3. The app may be a Standard Navigation Target, not a directly launchable tile

Per KBA 3740429, some apps are categorised as Standard Navigation Target (App Category T) — meaning they cannot be launched as a standalone tile from the launchpad or found via search. They must be accessed via navigation from a parent app.

Check: In the Business Catalogs app, open SAP_LE_BC_ID_PROC_MC and look at the Applications tab. If VL31N has category T, it will not appear as a search result or tile.

4. Starter system limitations

The SUPER YOU Starter System is a limited, pre-scoped demo environment. Some scope items may not be activated by design. If 2TX is not part of the pre-configured scope, activating it may not be possible without SAP involvement.

Recommended next step: Check the Manage Your Solution app (if available) to see which scope items are active. If 2TX is absent, raise this with your SAP contact or Learning Hub support for the starter system.

Suggested Workaround in the Meantime

If VL31N is unavailable in the starter system, the functionally equivalent app for PO-based inbound delivery creation is:

  • Inbound Deliveries for Purchase Orders (VL34) — creates inbound deliveries for one or multiple POs, selected by delivery date. This app is typically available under the same scope item and business catalog.

Sources:

  • KBA 3536797 – Missing business catalog SAP_LE_BC_ID_PROC_MC: link
  • KBA 3499342 – Apps not found after catalog assignment: link
  • KBA 3462922 – Missing catalogs when scope item not activated: link
  • KBA 3740429 – App category Standard Navigation Target: link

entry.title: Organizational Structure in SAP TM
entry.content:
TM has its own org model:
If you know S/4HANA, you know company codes, plants and sales areas. TM doesn’t reuse that setup as is. It has its own org model, which you can build to match ERP or keep separate.

What it represents

In SAP TM

In S/4HANA

The legal entity and its currency

Company organization

Company code

The team that sells logistics services

Sales organization, office, group

Sales organization (part of a sales area)

The team that buys from carriers

Purchasing organization, group

Purchasing organization, group

The team that plans and dispatches

Planning and execution organization, group

No match

Distribution channel and division

Not used, only defaulted in settings

Part of the sales area

One thing surprises people TM has no direct link to finance objects like company codes or cost centers. The company organization is mapped to the company code, and the actual financial posting happens back in S/4HANA or your billing system.

The building blocks:
SAP TM has three main types of org unit, and each one shows up on its own documents:

Org typeWhat it doesWhere you see it

Sales

Sells transport services to customers

Forwarding quotations, forwarding orders, customer contracts, forwarding settlements

Purchasing

Buys capacity from carriers and forwarders

Freight orders, freight bookings, service orders, freight agreements, freight settlements

Planning and execution (P&E)

Plans loads, dispatches and runs the moves

Freight units, transportation units, freight orders, freight bookings, resources

There’s also a fourth option, the forwarding house. It’s one unit that sells, buys and plans, which is common for logistics service providers (LSPs).

Every org unit gets two settings:

  • Function says what the unit does: sales, purchasing, planning and execution, company, corporate or forwarding house.
  • Role says where it sits in the tree: organization, office or group.

You can’t combine these freely. TM fixes which roles can sit under which:

Fig: SAP TM org hierarchy

Sales is the only type with three levels organization, then office, then group. Purchasing and P&E skip the office, so groups hang directly under the organization.

Example: Meridian Cargo Solutions
To make this concrete, I built a small structure for a made-up logistics company, Meridian Cargo Solutions. Here’s what it looks like in the system:


Fig: The Meridian Cargo Solutions org structure in SAP TM


Flow:
- Corporate MCS is the top node. It’s optional, but it gives you one place to start.
- Meridian Cargo Solutions is the company organization, the TM version of the company code.
- Sales Org EU and Sales Org US sell services. Sales Org US has a Sales Office East Coast, and under it a Sales Group Sea Freight.
- Purchasing Org Global buys from carriers. It has two groups, EU and US, and a Purchasing Team Lead position held by Tom York.
- Planning and Execution Global plans and runs the shipments.

Inside an org unit: the Org data tab
Click any unit and open the Org. data tab. This is where TM keeps the settings that matter most. Here’s Sales Office East Coast:

Fig: Org data tab for Sales Office East Coast, showing function, role and business partner

  • Org. Unit Function = Sales. This unit belongs to the sales side.
  • Org. Unit Role = Office. It sits at the office level, between the sales org and the sales group.
  • Business Partner = 1001620. TM created this business partner automatically when the unit was saved.

That last point is easy to miss. Every org unit gets its own business partner in the background, and that business partner is what appears on your orders. For this to work, the business partner number range and grouping need to be set up in Customizing.

People and workflow: positions
Org units describe teams. Positions describe the people in them. You need positions when TM has to send work to someone, for example an approval or an error to fix.
In the example, Purchasing Org Global has a Purchasing Team Lead position, and Tom York (user YORKTO) is its holder:

           

Fig: The Purchasing Team Lead position with Tom York as holder

  • Head of own organizational unit is ticked, so Tom York is the head of Purchasing Org Global. Workflow uses this to know who approves.
  • Staffing status says the position is occupied.

A few common roles you might set up this way:

PersonAssigned to

Tendering manager

Purchasing org

Sales manager who checks credit limits

Sales org

Purchasing agent who checks carrier invoices

Purchasing org

Planners, drivers, loading clerks, warehouse staff

Planning and execution org

A holder can be an SAP user, an HR person or a business partner with the employee role. In my demo system, I used an SAP user, which works fine for workflow.

Steps to follow:

What you want to doWhere to do it

Create a new structure

Transaction PPOCE, or SPRO › Transportation Management › Master Data › Organizational Management › Organizational Model › Create Organizational Model

Change an existing structure

Transaction PPOME, or the same path › Change Organizational Model

Copy a structure from S/4HANA or ERP

Report /SCMTMS/TRANS_ORG_MODEL (Create and Merge Organizational Hierarchy)

Set default distribution channel and division

SPRO › Transportation Management › Master Data › Basic Functions › General Settings › Define General Settings for SAP TM

Set up business partner numbering for org units

SPRO › Cross-Application Components › SAP Business Partner › Business Partner › Basic Settings › Number Ranges and Groupings

The basic steps in PPOCE are:

  1. Create the top unit and give it a code and a name.
  2. On the Org. data tab, click Create, then pick the function and role.
  3. Select the unit, click Create, and choose “Is line supervisor of” to add a unit under it. Repeat down the tree.
  4. For a position, choose “Incorporates” instead. Then use Assign › Holder to link a user or person.
  5. Save. TM creates the business partners at this point.

If your structure already exists in S/4HANA, the import report saves time. It reads the source hierarchy, lets you drag the parts you want across, and creates them in TM. After saving, you make any changes in the org model itself.

Conclusion
The org structure in SAP TM is small, but everything else builds on it. Keep three things in mind: TM has its own model, separate from finance; the function and role decide what each unit is and where it can sit and every unit becomes a business partner on your documents. Set it up cleanly once and your orders, charges and approvals will follow.

entry.title: SII Spain: error 3019 when reversing an invoice from a closed period
entry.content:
Dear community,

I’m working with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and the Spanish SII (received invoices, daily submission), and I’ve run into the following case. I’d appreciate it if anyone who has solved it could share their experience.

Scenario: A supplier invoice is posted and submitted to the SII in period A (closed, with the VAT return already filed). Later, the invoice has to be reversed for accounting reasons, and the reversal is posted in period B (open). The invoice is then re-posted correctly in period B.

Problem:

  • If the reversal inherits the original tax reporting date, a deregistration request is generated pointing to period A. The customer does not want a filed period to be modified.
  • If I change the tax reporting date of the reversal document to period B, the submission fails with error 3019: “El Ejercicio y Periodo del PeriodoLiquidacion deben coincidir con el último movimiento anterior”.

Customer requirement: The correction should be reported in the current period with the opposite sign, without manual intervention in the SII, so that the books match what has been reported. The same process should also work when the reversal falls in the same period as the original invoice.

What I have checked: The configuration activity for handling reversal documents (102954) offers the options “Send deregistration or set status cancelled”, “Always send deregistration” and “Send new invoice with type F1/F2/R1/R1S/R2/R2S/R3/R3S”. However, the setting is fixed per company code and document type, so it cannot distinguish between same-period and different-period reversals.

Questions:

  1. Has anyone encountered error 3019 in this scenario, and how did you solve it?
  2. Does sending the reversal as a new invoice (F1/R1) with the current period’s tax reporting date avoid the error in practice?
  3. Is there a way for the standard to send a deregistration for same-period reversals and an opposite-sign entry for reversals of closed periods?

Thanks in advance.

entry.title: Re: Replace FIFO-assigned batches in outbound delivery (b...
entry.content:
I reproduced all three on an S/4HANA 2023 system, calling BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CHANGE with HEADER_CONTROL-SIMULATE = 'X' and no commit. They come from two different places: the quantity check, and the path that NEW_ITEM_DATA takes.

1. VLBAPI 004 is the quantity check, and the real cause is the next line in RETURN

For each ITEM_DATA line that has a quantity or a sales unit, the BAPI runs the form QUANTITY_CHECK (function group V50I), which calls SHP_QUANTITY_CONSISTENCY_CHECK. When it fails, the BAPI writes VLBAPI 004 ("Error in document &1 item &2 (quantity consistency check)") and right after it a second line with the error raised by the check itself (a VL 26x number). What I measured on one delivery item:

  • DLV_QTY, DLV_QTY_IMUNIT, SALES_UNIT and BASE_UOM filled, FACT_UNIT_NOM and FACT_UNIT_DENOM empty: E VLBAPI 004, then VL 268 with 0 and 0 in V1 and V2 ("Conversion factors &1:&2 are zero, not defined mathematically").
  • The same call with FACT_UNIT_NOM = 1 and FACT_UNIT_DENOM = 1: RETURN came back empty.
  • The VL 268 line came with TYPE W, not E, and the text field was empty on both lines (only ID, NUMBER and V1 to V4). If you read only the E lines, you see VLBAPI 004 and lose the cause.

So every ITEM_DATA line with a quantity needs FACT_UNIT_NOM and FACT_UNIT_DENOM, taken from LIPS-UMVKZ and LIPS-UMVKN of that item, with DLV_QTY and DLV_QTY_IMUNIT consistent with them. The check is skipped only when all quantities and the sales unit are empty, so a line that changes only BATCH on an existing sub item does not run it (I did not test that variant).

2. /SPE/DIRDLV 006 and 014 come from the path NEW_ITEM_DATA takes

When NEW_ITEM_DATA is filled, the form DET_DIRDLV_AND_PROCESS sends the change to /SPE/OUTB_DELIVERY_CHANGE_INT (the decentralized EWM delivery processing) instead of WS_DELIVERY_UPDATE, as long as CL_OPS_SWITCH_CHECK=>LE_SFWS_SC3 returns true. It did in my system. That path needs two things:

  • NEW_ITEM_ORG with plant and storage location, in a line with the same DELIV_NUMB and ITM_NUMBER as the NEW_ITEM_DATA line. The form SPE_NEW_ITEM_FILL reads NEW_ITEM_ORG by those two fields, and when it finds no line, or a line with STGE_LOC empty, it raises E /SPE/DIRDLV 006 ("No storage location is assigned to delivery item &1"). I got the 006 with STGE_LOC empty, and also with STGE_LOC filled but DELIV_NUMB empty or another ITM_NUMBER in NEW_ITEM_ORG.
  • A warehouse number in T320 for that plant and storage location. With a storage location that has no T320 entry I got E /SPE/DIRDLV 014 ("No warehouse number is assigned to plant &1 and storage location &2"), which is checked in /SPE/DETERMINE_DELIVERY_TYPE and /SPE/DETERMINE_ITEM_CATEG.

In your second try you mention ITEM_DATA and ITEM_ORG, but this BAPI has no ITEM_ORG parameter, and the only place I found the 006 raised in function group V50I is SPE_NEW_ITEM_FILL, for a NEW_ITEM_DATA line. So your add went down this path, which matches what you saw: 006 without STGE_LOC, and 014 with it, because your storage location has no warehouse number. With such a storage location this path stops at the 014, as in my test, so the way out is the ITEM_DATA route below. I did not test VL02N, but these checks sit in the BAPI flow, which fits with VL02N working for you.

3. The batch split sub item goes in ITEM_DATA, not in NEW_ITEM_DATA

In the form MAP2I_BAPIOBDLVITEMCHG_VBPOK, when USEHIERITM is the batch sub item value ('1' in domain HIEVW, "Batch Subitem"), the BAPI fills VBPOK with POSNR_VL = HIERARITEM (the main item) and WMS_RFPOS and WMS_RFBEL = your DELIV_ITEM. The code comment there says "Save batch split sub item". SAP's own unit test in that function group (class LTCL_V50I_ER25, method SPE_VBPOK_OBDLV_FILL_2) sends exactly that, item 900001 with a batch, HIERARITEM 000010 and USEHIERITM for batch sub item, and expects VBPOK with POSNR_VL 000010 and WMS_RFPOS 900001. So what I would try, in a single call:

  • ITEM_DATA for each sub item you keep or add: DELIV_ITEM = sub item number, HIERARITEM = main item, USEHIERITM = '1', MATERIAL, BATCH, DLV_QTY, DLV_QTY_IMUNIT, SALES_UNIT, BASE_UOM, FACT_UNIT_NOM and FACT_UNIT_DENOM.
  • ITEM_CONTROL with CHG_DELQTY = 'X' for those lines, and DEL_ITEM = 'X' for the FIFO sub items you want to drop.
  • First with SIMULATE = 'X' (the code then sets the database update to checks only), then the real call, and BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT only if RETURN has no E or A line. With everything in one call and that rule, a delete is never saved without the add.

That also answers WS_DELIVERY_UPDATE_2: the BAPI already builds the VBPOK line for the sub item, so I would try this before calling the update function directly.

4. Batch at creation

BAPI_OUTB_DELIVERY_CREATE_SLS cannot take it: its item table (BAPIDLVREFTOSALESORDER) has REF_DOC, REF_ITEM, DLV_QTY, SALES_UNIT and a few reference fields, and no batch field. The options I know are the batch already on the sales order item, or no automatic batch determination for the delivery item category (TVLP-CHAUT) and then the change call above. I did not test either.

What I did not test: a real batch replacement on an open batch split item (my system has no delivery with batch split), how the delivery update handles WMS_RFPOS for a new sub item, and the two creation options. The three errors, the fix for VLBAPI 004 and the three ways to get the 006 are measured.

entry.title: E-learning Available: Driving Finance Transformation by Converting to SAP S/4HANA
entry.content:
For many organisations running SAP ERP, the journey to SAP S/4HANA represents far more than a technical upgrade - it is a fundamental transformation of the finance function. Legacy ERP finance architectures rely on separate data structures for financial accounting, controlling, and asset accounting, requiring complex reconciliation processes, batch-driven reporting cycles, and significant manual effort during period-end close. These constraints limit real-time financial visibility, slow down decision-making, and create a growing gap between what the business needs and what the finance organization can deliver.

Converting to SAP S/4HANA Finance offers the opportunity to fundamentally re-architect how financial data is captured, processed, and reported - unlocking real-time insights, simplifying the data model, and enabling a faster, more intelligent close. To help finance professionals, project team members, and consultants navigate this transformation, this 1.5-hour e-learning course guides learners through the essential finance changes, conversion activities, and data migration steps involved in moving to SAP S/4HANA Finance.

entry.title: What’s New in Identity and Access Management in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
entry.content:
1.  Overview

Identity and Access Management (IAM) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition provides the foundational security layer that controls user access to business applications and backend services. Traditionally, IAM apps were grouped into business catalogs, with authorization default values aggregated strictly at the catalog level. These business catalogs served as the essential building blocks for constructing business roles. The traditional authorization flow works as follows:

Business Role  →  Business Catalog  →  Fiori→  Authorization Defaults / Services

While this catalog-centric model provided a straightforward way to bundle related apps, it operated on an "all-or-nothing" principle. Assigning a catalog granted access to every application within it.

To solve these limitations, SAP evolved the IAM architecture from rigid catalog bundles to modular application entities.

2.  What Is "App as Entity"?

Starting with Release 2502, SAP introduced “App Authorization Variants” for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. An App Authorization Variant acts as a standalone wrapper around an application's authorization requirements, decoupling it from the catalog to make the individual IAM App -rather than the catalog- the smallest assignable unit of authorization.

With Release 2608, this capability expands into the broader "App as Entity" framework, enabling administrators to directly assign, toggle active/inactive, and manage application access with fine-grained precision when building Business Roles.

The diagram below illustrates this shift from broad catalog bundling to standalone, app-level role construction.

2.1  The Challenges of the Catalog-Only Approach

While catalogs provide great pre-bundled workplaces, relying solely on them introduced friction:

  • Inability to create business roles for a specific subset of apps without custom catalog creation.
  • High change-management effort when catalogs required splitting due to evolving requirements.
  • Automatic exposure of newly added apps to end-users upon upgrades, along with their underlying authorizations.

By shifting to "App as Entity," administrators can now assemble roles based on exact user tasks without rigid constraints, enabling the direct launch of all application types via assigned transaction codes in S/4HANA Public Edition and SAP BTP, ABAP environment.

2.2  Practical Scenarios:

  • User Management: Grant user access to the Business User app without exposing access to the Business Roles app.
  • Procurement: Assign access to a specific Purchase Order app without granting permissions to all applications inside the broader Procurement catalog.

3.  How App Assignment Works

"App as Entity" does not replace Business Catalogs. Instead, Business Catalogs and direct app selection run side-by-side in parallel.

When configuring a role in the Maintain Business Roles Fiori app (F1492), administrators now have two assignment mechanisms:

Assignment Type

How It Works

Best Used For

Assigned via Business Catalog

The Business Catalog is assigned to the Business Role. IAM Apps within that catalog can be selectively activated or deactivated and are part of the resulting role accordingly.

Standard role setup where a user needs the complete suite of applications in a functional area.

Direct Assignment

An App Authorization Variant /IAM App is selected directly for a Business Role without requiring the overarching Business Catalog to be assigned.

Granular role setup where a user needs only 1 or 2 specific applications from a larger domain.

3.1  In-App Granular Control

Beyond assigning broad Business Catalogs, administrators can now manage application access with pinpoint accuracy. The Maintain Business Roles app (F1492) allows security leads to directly add, remove, toggle, or inspect individual IAM Apps to match exact user job responsibilities.

3.1.1  Practical Example: Direct App Selection in Action

To see how "App as Entity" works in practice, consider configuring the "Internal Sales Representative" role as an example inside the Maintain Business Roles app.

As shown in the screenshot above, administrators are no longer limited to managing entire catalogs. Instead, the dedicated IAM Apps tab allows granular control over individual applications:

  • Direct App Authorization Variants: Specific apps, such as Display Business Partner, Display Customer (Centrally), or Supplier are assigned directly as "App Authorization Variants" with their linked transaction objects.
  • Selection & Activation Control: Checkboxes alongside each IAM App let administrators select specific items to Add, Remove, Activate, or Deactivate permissions without affecting the rest of the business domain.
  • Catalog-Free Flexibility: Notice that this role has 0 Business Catalogs assigned yet contains 27 IAM Apps assigned directly. This proves that roles can now be built using standalone app entities tailored to exact job tasks.

3.1.2  Toggling Apps ON/OFF

In addition to Direct Assignment, administrators can open an assigned Business Catalog inside the Maintain Business Roles app (F1492) and toggle individual IAM Apps ON or OFF.

 Important Note on Toggling:

Toggling an app OFF inside F1492 suppresses its underlying authorization defaults for that specific Business Role instance only. It does NOT alter or remove the app definition from the underlying Business Catalog in ABAP Development Tools (ADT), preserving the central catalog definition for other roles.


4.  Application Scope: SAP Standard vs. Customer-Developed Apps

The "App as Entity" model applies to both SAP-delivered content and custom-built extensions:

4.1  SAP Standard Applications

As introduced in Section 2, SAP delivers standard content pre-configured as individual App Authorization Variants (SIA6 objects).

For standard applications, this eliminates the need to assign full standard catalogs. Security administrators can directly select individual SAP standard apps when building Business Roles, ensuring users receive access only to the exact standard functionality required for their tasks while avoiding the overhead of creating custom catalogs in ADT.

4.2  Customer-Developed Applications (Developer Extensibility)

Custom applications built via ABAP Cloud / ADT using the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) are defined as External IAM Apps (SIA6 objects).

  • The Migration Requirement: To enable custom apps for individual selection in Business Roles, existing customer IAM Apps (SIA6) and their corresponding Business Catalogs (GBAK objects) must undergo a one-time migration using the built-in migration wizard in ABAP Development Tools (ADT).
  • The Outcome: Once migrated, customer-developed apps can participate in direct assignments and individual toggling just like SAP standard applications.


5  On-Premise (PFCG) to Cloud IAM Migration Realities

A common question during cloud transformation projects is whether existing On-Premise PFCG roles can be migrated directly into S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

5.1  Key Architectural Differences

Feature

On-Premise (PFCG)

S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (IAM)

Primary Building Block

Transactions (TCODES), Auth Objects, & Profiles

IAM Apps (SIA6), Business Catalogs, & Business Roles

Menu Maintenance

Direct TCode insertion in PFCG Menu tab

IAM Apps bundled in Business Catalogs via ADT

Authorization Abstraction

Direct maintenance of Auth Objects & Fields in SU24

Managed via IAM Apps, Business Catalogs, and Restriction Types

5.2  Migration Reality

Because On-Premise PFCG roles lack the underlying IAM App metadata layer (SIA6 objects), there is no automated 1-to-1 role import tool.

  • Best Practice: Customers migrating from On-Premise to S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition must construct their business roles using standard SAP reference catalogs or custom IAM Apps created in ADT.


6  Key Takeaways

  • Greater Flexibility: Security teams can build roles aligned with real user job descriptions using Direct Assignment or Catalog-based Assignment.
  • Reduced Customization: Eliminates the need to build redundant custom catalogs in ADT just to exclude a single application.
  • Segregation of Duties (SoD) Preserved: Business Catalogs remain the standard for grouping apps and preserving regularly audited SoD compliance. App as Entity adds fine-grained flexibility on top of this foundation.
  • Migration Needed for Custom Content: Existing customer-developed IAM Apps (SIA6) and catalogs (GBAK) must be migrated via the ADT wizard to participate in direct assignment.


7  More to read:

To dive deeper, explore the following official resources and reference guides:

  • Identity and Access Management (IAM)
  • Maintain Business Roles (Fiori App F1492)
  • Creating an IAM App for the Business Service
  • IAM Information System App (F2450) Usage Guide

SQL Server Upgrade Impact for Tricentis Tosca 2025

Important Note: The available SAP documentation covers SQL Server upgrades in the context of SAP NetWeaver-based systems. Tricentis Tosca is a test automation tool that integrates with SAP Solution Manager, and its specific SQL Server compatibility matrix should be verified directly with Tricentis/SAP support. The guidance below reflects SAP's documented SQL Server 2025 upgrade considerations and known edition-related issues that are relevant to your planning.

Compatibility Considerations
  • No accepted answer exists yet for the specific question of Tricentis Tosca 2025 compatibility with SQL Server 2025 — the community thread matching your exact scenario (Tosca 2025 + SQL Server 2022 Enterprise → SQL Server 2025 Standard) was posted on 10-09-2026 and currently has 0 accepted solutions and 0 answers. [1] You should raise a formal SAP support ticket to obtain a definitive compatibility statement before proceeding.
  • SAP's official documentation confirms that SQL Server 2025 upgrade is supported from SQL Server 2022 (16.x) as a valid upgrade path, and SQL Server 2022 users do not need to apply any additional SPS (Support Package Stack) before upgrading to SQL Server 2025. [2]
  • SQL Server 2025 is only available for 64-bit platforms; cross-platform upgrades are not supported. [3]
Enterprise → Standard Edition: Key Impacts
Area Enterprise Edition Standard Edition
DBCON / ABAP Connectivity (EngineEdition)EngineEdition = 3 (required by DBSL library for MSSQL_SE=1 connections)EngineEdition = 2 — DBSL library will reject the connection with error: "The DBSL library supports only connections to the SQL Server Database Engine with the Engine Edition = 3" [4]
Edition Downgrade PathEnterprise → Standard is a supported edition upgrade path in SQL Server 2025 [3] [5]Standard edition is a valid target, but feature availability must be verified before downgrading
High Availability FeaturesFull HA features (AlwaysOn AG, Failover Clustering) supportedSome HA features are limited or unavailable in Standard Edition — verify your HA topology [3]
Feature CompatibilityFull Enterprise feature setVerify that all features currently in use are supported in Standard Edition before proceeding [6]

⚠️ Critical Warning on Edition Change: SAP KBA 3739963 explicitly documents that when connecting an ABAP system to an external SQL Server 2025 Standard Developer edition (EngineEdition = 2), the DBSL library blocks the connection because it only supports EngineEdition = 3 (Enterprise). [4] While this KBA specifically references the "Standard Developer edition," the underlying EngineEdition = 2 applies to Standard edition as well. You must confirm with SAP Support whether the Standard (non-Developer) edition of SQL Server 2025 is supported for your specific Tosca/SAP integration before proceeding with the edition downgrade.

Prerequisites & Precautions
  1. Verify SAP Note 3649352: Confirm the minimum recommended SPS level for SQL Server 2025 compatibility with your SAP/Tosca landscape. Since you are on SQL Server 2022, no additional SPS is required prior to the SQL Server upgrade itself, but the minimum SPS for SQL Server 2025 must still be met. [2]
  2. Import latest SAP kernel patches and dbsl library: Ensure the latest kernel patches, dbsl library, and support package stacks are applied at or above the minimum level specified for SQL Server 2025. These are available on the SAP Support Portal under Software Downloads (see SAP Note 19466). [2]
  3. Verify feature usage vs. Standard Edition: Before downgrading from Enterprise to Standard, confirm that every SQL Server feature currently used by Tosca and any connected SAP systems is supported in Standard Edition. [3] [6]
  4. Check for pending restarts: The SQL Server 2025 upgrade will be blocked if there is a pending system restart, if the Windows Installer Service is not running, or if performance counters are corrupt. [2]
  5. Confirm 64-bit environment: SQL Server 2025 is only supported on 64-bit platforms. [3]
  6. Confirm Windows OS compatibility: SQL Server 2025 installation requires Windows Server 2019 Standard/Datacenter or Windows Server 2022 Standard/Datacenter. [7]
  7. Raise an SAP Support ticket: Given the open community question with no accepted answer [1], formally engage SAP Support (category: SOLMAN Test Suite / SAP Solution Manager) to obtain a certified compatibility statement for Tosca 2025 with SQL Server 2025 Standard Edition.
  8. Full database backup: Take a complete backup of all databases before initiating any upgrade activity. [8] [2]
Recommended Upgrade Steps
  1. Perform a full backup of all databases and verify backup integrity before starting.
  2. Shut down the SAP/Tosca application before beginning the SQL Server upgrade. [2]
  3. Apply latest SAP kernel patches and dbsl library to meet the SQL Server 2025 minimum requirements (SAP Note 3649352 and SAP Note 19466).
  4. Run the SQL Server 2025 setup and select "Upgrade from a previous version of SQL Server" — follow the prompts, specifying the correct instance. Note: You cannot use the SQL4SAP script to upgrade from SQL Server 2022 to SQL Server 2025; the SQL4SAP script does not support this upgrade path. [7]
  5. Post-SQL upgrade verification: Confirm the SQL Server version, check SQL Server error logs for any errors, and test database connectivity. [8]
  6. Perform the edition change (Enterprise → Standard) as a separate step after the version upgrade is confirmed stable, following Microsoft's "Upgrade to a different edition of SQL Server (Setup)" procedure. [3] [5]
  7. Restart the SAP/Tosca system and validate that all services are running correctly, all Tosca test connections are functional, and run a regression check. [8]
  8. Develop a rollback plan before starting — ensure you can restore the original SQL Server 2022 Enterprise environment if issues arise. [9]

entry.title: Re: Processing RFC Queues errors on EWM SAP Public Cloud
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question. Here's the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Joule Response

Reprocessing qRFC in SAP EWM Public Cloud
Issue Summary

You have a stuck qRFC queue (DLWS0M8E6E4 0080000423) in SAP EWM Public Cloud with the error:

Command to tRFC/qRFC: Execute LUW again — Message no. /SCWM/MONITOR064

This message is classified by SAP as "self-explanatory," but in practice it does not reveal the underlying root cause directly. The real error is often hidden behind this generic status, and the queue remains in RETRY state. [1]

Resolution Steps

Step 1: Verify Queue Status via Dashboard Messages Tile

Since you found no queues in the Dashboard Messages tile, the queue may not be surfacing there due to how Public Cloud exposes qRFC errors. Instead, navigate directly to the Warehouse Monitor:

  • Go to /SCWM/MON → Tools → Message Queue
  • Locate the stuck queue (DLWS* prefix)
  • Check the error status and attempt reprocessing from there [2]

Step 2: Attempt Debug LUW in the Monitor

Per SAP KBA 3555285, the "Execute LUW again" message can sometimes appear because the application log is too large to display — not necessarily because there is a real blocking error. The recommended action is: [3]

  1. Click the Debug LUW button on the stuck queue
  2. Press F8 to execute
  3. If no error appears during execution, the queue may actually process successfully
  4. If an error does appear, set a breakpoint on function module /SCWM/TO_CREATE_WHR and check variable lt_bapiret for the actual error detail [3]

Step 3: Check SLG1 Application Log

Even if the queue monitor shows no detail, check transaction SLG1 for application logs around the timestamp of the queue failure. Filter by the queue name or the user ID associated with the stuck queue. This often reveals the true blocking error (e.g., authorization issue, lock conflict, or customizing gap). [4] [5]

Step 4: Check for Authorization Issues (SU53)

A common hidden cause for this error is a missing authorization. After the queue failure, run transaction SU53 with the user that triggered the queue. If a missing authorization object is displayed, assign it and then reprocess the queue. [6]

Step 5: Engage SAP Support

Since you are on SAP EWM Public Cloud, direct queue debugging (e.g., production debug access) is restricted. If the above steps do not resolve the issue: [7] [5]

  • Raise a support case under component SCM-EWM-DLP (Delivery Processing) or SCM-EWM-WOP (Warehouse Order Processing), depending on the queue type
  • Reference KBA 3258037 (WMDPDO/WMDPDI queues in RETRY with SR053) and KBA 3555285 (WM* queue with "Execute LUW again") in your case
  • SAP Support will debug the queue in the production environment to identify the exact root cause [8] [9]
Key Considerations

Quantity Adjustment Impact on S/4HANA Sync

  • You adjusted the quantity to 0 on the EWM side, but the S/4HANA side has not yet received this update — this is precisely because the qRFC carrying the confirmation is stuck.
  • Until the queue is successfully processed (or cleared by SAP Support), the two systems will remain out of sync.
  • Do not manually force-delete the queue without SAP Support guidance, as this can cause permanent data inconsistencies between EWM and S/4HANA. [2]

Known Limitation in EWM Public Cloud for qRFC Reprocessing

  • In the Public Cloud environment, standard on-premise tools like direct SMQ1/SMQ2 access and production debugging are not available to customers — this is a confirmed constraint, which is why the SAP Community thread you referenced advises contacting SAP Support. [7]
  • The Warehouse Monitor (/SCWM/MON → Tools → Message Queue) is the primary self-service tool available in Public Cloud for queue visibility and reprocessing attempts. [2] [10]
  • If the queue cannot be reprocessed via the monitor, SAP Support is the required escalation path for Public Cloud environments.

entry.title: Re: defective quantity on api API_QUALITYNOTIFICATION
entry.content:
You are right, there is no such field on the header. I checked on an S/4HANA 2023 system: the header entity of API_QUALITYNOTIFICATION has no quantity field at all, and the defective quantities exist only on the item.

What I measured

  • The header entity QualityNotification is the CDS view A_QltyNotification, a projection on R_QltyNotificationTP. It has type, texts, codes, dates, supplier, customer, material, plant, purchasing data, inspection lot, batch and material document, and no quantity.
  • The business object under it already knows two header quantities: its behavior maps NotificationComplaintQuantity to QMEL-RKMNG and NotificationExternalQty to QMEL-MGFRD (Defective Quantity (External)). The internal one, QMEL-MGEIG, is not even in that view. The API projection exposes none of them.
  • A_QltyNotification is released only for remote use (C2). The extension contract (C0) is not released and the projection behavior is not marked extensible, so you cannot add the standard field to the API with developer extensibility.
  • The header behavior only allows create, no update, so this API cannot change header fields of an existing notification anyway.
  • The item entity QualityNotificationItem has ExternalDefectiveQuantity (QMFE-FMGFRD) and InternalDefectiveQuantity (QMFE-FMGEIG). DefectiveQuantityUnit is read only.

I also ran it: I created a Q2 notification through the API business object (EML on A_QltyNotification, no commit, rolled back) with one item with ExternalDefectiveQuantity 3 and InternalDefectiveQuantity 1. FAILED was empty, REPORTED returned no texts, and reading the item back gave 3 and 1. The unit came back empty: it is read only, and I did not test when it gets filled.

What you can do

  • Inside this API, the item is the only place for a defective quantity.
  • On premise or private cloud, if it must be the header: QMEL-MGFRD and QMEL-MGEIG are in the header structure RIQS5 of the RFC function module IQS4_CREATE_NOTIFICATION. I called it with I_POST = space, so nothing was saved. With the default I_CHECK_PARNR_COMP = 'X' it stopped with error IX 200 for partner functions KU (Coordinator) and LF (Supplier, VN on English screens), which are mandatory for Q2 in my system. With I_CHECK_PARNR_COMP = space the header came back with a temporary number, RKMNG 10, MGFRD 5 and MGEIG 2. In a real call, pass the partners in I_IHPA_T instead of switching the check off.
  • This function module is not a released API, so it is for classic ABAP or RFC only. BAPI_QUALNOT_CREATE does not help here: its header (BAPI2078_NOTHDRI) has QUANT_COMPLAINT for the complaint quantity, and no defective quantity.
  • The field documentation says external plus internal must not exceed the complaint quantity. In my run the function module did not check that before save: 8 and 5 against a complaint quantity of 10 came back with no error. If you go this way, check it on your side.
  • If you are on the public cloud, open the $metadata of your service and look at the QualityNotification entity: if it has no quantity property, it is the same situation, and the item is the way.

What I did not test: saving the notification in either path, passing the partners in I_IHPA_T, calling the OData service over HTTP, the maintenance notification API you mentioned, and releases after 2023 or the public cloud. The API fields, the mapping and the runs above are measured.
